inspirations.title: Inspirations
inspirations.intro: People and work that left fingerprints.

directors.title: Directors
directors.description: Framing, silence, rhythm and the courage to let a scene be strange.

items.label: Jiang Wen
items.note: Satire, cultural layering and the ability to make chaos feel completely deliberate.

items.label: Quentin Tarantino
items.note: Dialogue as violence; rhythm as narrative.

items.label: Stanley Kubrick
items.note: Precision, geometry and dread — every frame feels loaded.

items.label: Takeshi Kitano
items.note: Violence, stillness and poetic disconnection.

items.label: David Fincher
items.note: Cold, obsessive, surgical storytelling.

games.title: Games
games.description: Games that made atmosphere, systems or memory feel more important than spectacle.

items.label: Life Is Strange
items.note: Choices, mood and music — one of those games where everything emotionally clicks.

items.label: P.T
items.note: The scariest hallway ever made. Minimal space, maximum pressure.

items.label: Metal Gear
items.note: Story colliding with systems, politics and wonderfully unnecessary ideas.

items.label: Cyberpunk 2077
items.note: The city as a character; neon future as melancholy.

music.title: Artists
music.description: Artists whose sound keeps leaking into how I think about texture, space, rhythm and emotion.

items.label: Tame Impala
items.note: Psychedelic texture, bass lines and distortion that still knows how to groove.

items.label: JPEGMAFIA
items.note: Noise, glitches and ugly sounds arranged with ridiculous intention.

items.label: Mk.gee
items.note: Warped guitars, negative space and songs that feel half-broken but completely alive.

items.label: Porter Robinson
items.note: Electronic music with sincerity at its core. Nurture made vulnerability feel enormous.

items.label: Flume
items.note: Digital artefacts turned into musical texture.

items.label: Jack White
items.note: Raw electricity, compression and fuzz without sanding off the edges.

items.label: Radiohead
items.note: Anxiety, atmosphere and arrangement as architecture.

items.label: Dou Wei
items.note: From the claustrophobic rock of Black Dream to later ambient, experimental and improvisational work — always changing the language instead of repeating himself.

albums.title: Albums
albums.description: Twenty-five records I keep returning to. No numbers here — just the covers, the feeling, and a way back into each record.

items.label: InnerSpeaker
items.note: Fuzzed-out psych rock that feels sun-bleached, loose and endlessly replayable.

items.label: Kamikaze
items.note: Pure recoil: sharp flows, dense rhyme schemes and the feeling of rapping with the brakes cut.

items.label: Currents
items.note: A perfect pivot from psych rock into synth-pop without losing the strange edges.

items.label: good kid, m.A.A.d city
items.note: A coming-of-age film in album form — detailed, tense and unbelievably cohesive.

items.label: 范特西
items.note: Jay Chou’s early world-building at full strength: R&B, rap, melody and Chinese imagery in one language.

items.label: SCARING THE HOES
items.note: Sample chaos with absurd control; abrasive on the surface, ridiculously precise underneath.

items.label: Nurture
items.note: Huge electronic music built from small, vulnerable feelings.

items.label: 2014 Forest Hills Drive
items.note: Warm, direct and personal — a rap album that feels like going home to think clearly.

items.label: The Slim Shady LP
items.note: Cartoonishly dark, technically hungry and already unmistakably Eminem.

items.label: Lonerism
items.note: Isolation turned into colour: stranger, denser and more inward than the debut.

items.label: 黑梦
items.note: Cold, nocturnal Chinese alternative rock that still sounds genuinely alien.

items.label: My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy
items.note: Maximalist rap as theatre: enormous production, ego, collapse and spectacle in the same frame.

items.label: Nevermind
items.note: Songs this immediate should not feel this heavy — pop instinct buried under distortion and exhaustion.

items.label: The Off-Season
items.note: Cole in training-room mode: focused, technical and almost completely uninterested in decoration.

items.label: UNLOCKED
items.note: A compact rap cartoon: breakneck verses and Kenny Beats production that keeps changing shape.

items.label: Carrie & Lowell
items.note: Grief whispered so quietly that every detail lands harder.

items.label: IGOR
items.note: Heartbreak arranged like a warped soul record — funny, ugly, tender and obsessive at once.

items.label: Veteran
items.note: JPEGMAFIA turning overload into structure; ugly textures made weirdly addictive.

items.label: 新长征路上的摇滚
items.note: Chinese rock with a spine: direct, rhythmic, confrontational and historically impossible to ignore.

items.label: Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band
items.note: Studio imagination becoming part of the songwriting itself.

items.label: 幻听
items.note: Dou Wei moving past rock form into atmosphere, repetition and a more abstract kind of motion.

items.label: 浮躁
items.note: Restless, airy and experimental — Faye Wong sounding completely unconcerned with playing safe.

items.label: American Football
items.note: Clean guitars, impossible timing and the quiet ache that defined an entire branch of emo.

items.label: Snow
items.note: Wide-open folk-pop: soft voices, patient arrangements and the feeling of driving somewhere far away.

items.label: Music From Before the Storm
items.note: One of my favourite game OSTs — restrained, bruised and inseparable from Before the Storm’s memory.
